 Live Reporting
 Charlotte Coates
 Most recent Most popular 'Bruno, Bruno' published at 12:04 GMT 12:04 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 There are not many Manchester United fans in the away section at Stamford Bridge just now but there was an audible 'Bruno, Bruno' from them when Bruno Fernandes led the outfield players out for their warm-up.
 I suspect there will be a unified effort to get management, players and fans moving in the same direction at least for the start of today's game at Stamford Bridge.
 Manchester United are staring at the possibility of a nine-game winless streak in all competitions for the first time since 1988-89.

 Post published at 12:02 GMT 12:02 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Reuters Manchester United could end today in the Premier League bottom three, if results go against them. 
 That'd be a proper Halloween scare for the United fans. 
 31 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:58 GMT 11:58 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Manchester United are winless in their last eight games in all competitions (D3 L5). They last had a longer run in October/November 1988 with nine.

 Click 'Get Involved' on this page to have your say 
 Disappointing that Mainoo did not make it. Midfield will need a big step-up. Would have preferred Cunha instead of Mount. If we see 100% effort and the right attitude, it's possible. 100% support for Carrick no matter what.
 Alan, Spain 
 79 57 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Man Utd's last four Premier League results published at 11:54 GMT 11:54 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Manchester United's last four Premier League results don't make for pretty reading at all. Just the three points. 
 Throw in a 4-1 loss away at Como in the Champions League, too. 
 32 20 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Expect tough, and intense game' published at 11:52 GMT 11:52 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, speaking to TNT Sports: "We are back in Premier League mode, so it is the most important. 
 "For sure, today is a big one. We need a good game and a good performance."
 On Estevao starting: "Because he is ready, because he has been preparing and training well. Today he is needed, and we hope he enjoys his game and that he can have a good impact."
 On whether Morgan Rogers will be the main centre forward: "Too early to tell, so we will see. It could, but we have options."
 On Jordan Henderson's exclusion : "He is ill, no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday, and today he had a fever."
 On Man Utd : "We expect a tough game, and intense game against United. They are a big team and good players, so we will need our best."

 As a Utd fan, 3-0 Chelsea sadly.
 Dodd, Yorkshire 
 As a Liverpool fan, I want United to win today to keep Carrick in post for when we play them in three weeks as I'm confident we could take three points. Last thing we need is the new manager bounce.
 Ash, Yorkshire 
 137 122 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'No issues' between Carrick and Fernandes published at 11:48 GMT 11:48 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 It was a huge call from Manchester United boss Michael Carrick to drop captain Bruno Fernandes in the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth. 
 But the two have held clear the air talks and he is back in the starting XI this afternoon. 
 Media caption, Michael Carrick says 'no issues' with Bruno Fernandes
 25 26 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 This is how you do it published at 11:46 GMT 11:46 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 When the Manchester United squad arrived a few of the players came straight out and had a look at the pitch.
 Matheus Cunha wandered on with fellow Brazilian Andrey Santos and started pointing to the end where he scored the winner last season, as if to say 'this is what I did'.
 It was a superb finish from a Bruno Fernandes cut back.
 What United - and Michael Carrick - would give for a repeat of that today.
 79 48 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Henderson is out through illness published at 11:43 GMT 11:43 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport Chelsea reporter 
 Chelsea are beset with injuries before this one but there is the additional problem that Jordan Henderson is a surprise absentee through illness. 
 Romeo Lavia comes into his place in midfield after his first 90 minutes since joining Chelsea in the penalty shootout defeat at Liverpool on Wednesday. 
 Joao Pedro, Emiliano Martinez, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato, Reece James, Jamie Gittens and Aaron Anselmino are also out. 
 25 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 11:41 GMT 11:41 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' on this page to have your say 
 This game should be titled: 'The battle of the wasted billions'.
 Sid, Belfast 
 339 86 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A tough time results wise' published at 11:39 GMT 11:39 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Manchester United 
 Image source, PA Media Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, speaking to TNT Sports: "I think we have got a good balance within the group with that. We have had a tough time results wise, but the boys are going into this game with quite a clear mind and we know what to do.
 "More about us, and what we bring to the game ourselves. We can't control what they bring to the game. We have got to be the best version of us, if we're close to that, we will have a good chance of winning the game."
 47 31 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Fernandes cannot be the captain' published at 11:36 GMT 11:36 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Glenn Murray 
Former Brighton striker on Premier League Kick-Off 
 It is a football club that isn't united in their process. 
 We saw back in the day, where Jaap Stam released his book, and it was 72 hours later he was out of the door. There was one man in charge and that was Sir Alex Ferguson. 
 Managers have less power in a football club now because of the way they have been set up. You wonder who is going to be making the decisions at Manchester United.
 If I am the manager of a football club, you have got to act with integrity. 
 Your manager and captain are normally pretty in sync. 
 For me, Bruno Fernandes cannot be the captain of the football club. 
 235 77 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing

 As a Chelsea fan I’m delighted they stuck with Carrick. I think that probably says it all.
 Chris 
 203 93 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 It's glorious out at Stamford Bridge published at 11:31 GMT 11:31 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport Chelsea reporter 
 Image source, Reuters It's a warm, sunny day in west London for Chelsea versus Manchester United.
 This is Chelsea's last home game before Remembrance Sunday, so the Blues will pay tribute to former players who lost their lives in the two World Wars in the matchday programme.
 There will also be a pre-match Remembrance tribute, with Chelsea Pensioners from the Royal Hospital Chelsea leading out the teams and a display organised by fan group We Are The Shed.
 Supporters have been invited to take their seats early for the tributes.
 93 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved - Should Carrick have been sacked? published at 11:29 GMT 11:29 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' to have your say on this page 
 Right then, guys. Let's get right into it. 
 Have Manchester United made the correct decision in giving Michael Carrick a chance to turn his fortunes around or should he have been shown the door last week?
 323 123 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Back to the future for Carrick published at 11:27 GMT 11:27 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 Bruno Fernandes' return to the Manchester United starting line-up was virtually certain.
 However, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo getting picked is also a good move.
 It hints at a formation that was denied to head coach Michael Carrick at the start of the season, when Amad Diallo was ruled out through injury.
 With Benjamin Sesko injured, it is the front four from last term, with Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos paired in midfield behind.
 It worked last season. Carrick needs it to work today.
 100 46 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 The Premier League table published at 11:25 GMT 11:25 GMT 
 It's all square at the top again after Manchester City tasted defeat for the first time this season away at Aston Villa last week. 
 This is set to look completely different after the eight games we have today.

 Coming up in the Premier League today published at 11:22 GMT 11:22 GMT 
 We've got a bumper day of Premier League action with eight games to get excited by.
 And we're starting at Stamford Bridge with a massive game between Chelsea and Manchester United.
